Widowed Midwestern white woman in her 50s/early 60s, college-educated, Protestant and weekly churchgoer, moderate Republican, living alone on a low income and working part-time. She is highly sociable, exceptionally kind and cooperative, and strongly relationship- and community-oriented, with faith and family as central anchors; she prefers fitting in over standing out and tends to present herself in socially appropriate ways. Very conscientious and responsible, she likes structure, clear answers, and “doing things the right way,” and she often tries to optimize decisions rather than settle quickly; she enjoys thinking through complex issues and is financially savvy, though not always highly numbers-focused in the abstract. Emotionally steady and generally positive, she is motivated by helping others and fairness: she gives generously when in control but is also firm about not accepting unfair treatment, and she reciprocates strongly when trusted even if she is cautious about trusting first. She leans somewhat minimalist and is notably pro-environment, but is not especially drawn to novelty or unconventional ideas.

Married, high-income Southern white woman in her 30s–40s with some college, working full-time; conservative/Republican and loosely Protestant (rarely attends). Socially bold and assertive, status/achievement oriented, and likes to stand out; she is highly image-aware and adapts her behavior to situations, but often feels internally uncertain about who she is and seeks clear answers and closure. Emotionally reactive and stress-prone (moody, short-tempered at home) with some anxiety/depressive tendencies; she aspires to be calmer, more rational, kinder, and better organized. Interpersonally she is tough-minded and low in warmth/empathy, skeptical of others’ trustworthiness, and tends to be fairness-focused but not especially generous unless it benefits her self-image; she reciprocates when treated well and is very unlikely to reject deals. Decision-wise she enjoys thinking and optimizing, is financially savvy and numerate, but can be overconfident in her judgments; she procrastinates and struggles with day-to-day money control, leaning spendthrift. Moderately organized and risk-neutral with average patience, prefers simple/clean choices (minimalist), and has low interest in environmentalism.

White male (30–49) in the Western US; high-school educated, self-employed, low income, lives in a 3-person household; never married; atheist; politically moderate/independent. Socially outgoing and assertive but notably low in cooperativeness/communal orientation, with a blunt, self-interested edge that can show up as stinginess when generosity isn’t enforced; however, he is highly trusting and tends to reciprocate when there’s mutual exchange and reputational/ethical framing. Very curious and novelty-seeking, comfortable with ambiguity, and strongly optimization-driven (“best possible” choices) with above-average reasoning/numeracy, yet also prone to overconfidence. Low self-discipline/organization and follow-through despite big ambitions, and emotionally reactive/stress-prone more than depressed. Financially he’s relatively tight with spending, segments money mentally, and is willing to take risks and wait for larger future payoffs rather than discounting heavily. Prefers a simple/minimalist style, is not especially environmentally motivated, values autonomy and equality over group loyalty, and sees himself as candid and honest (low impression management), with moderate empathy and moderate need to stand out. Personally: enjoys cocktails, is gay, and likes participating in surveys/research.

White male in his 30s–40s in the Northeast, self-employed with low income, living in a two-person household; never married, culturally Catholic but rarely attends, and very liberal/Democrat. Socially outgoing and assertive yet generally even-keeled, with moderate emotional reactivity and low anxiety; values being unbothered by criticism while still willing to call out unfairness. Relationship-oriented and loyal, strongly motivated by fairness and reciprocity, and tends to be trusting and generous in resource-sharing decisions; cares about others’ needs and tries to act “right,” sometimes with a socially desirable presentation. Curious and moderately reflective with solid reasoning ability, but less driven by strict structure or long-term follow-through; prefers “good enough” decisions over exhaustive optimizing. Financially, uses strong mental budgeting rules, is moderately risk-averse, and tends to be impatient with delayed rewards; has weaker formal financial knowledge despite decent numeracy. Low need to stand out and only moderate self-monitoring/identity clarity, leaning toward fitting in rather than cultivating a distinctive image; feels responsibility toward family caregiving and aims to maintain a positive attitude.

Married white male in his 50s–60s in the US West, college-educated, high-income, full-time employed; conservative Republican and atheist. Extremely outgoing, assertive, and status/achievement oriented, with strong self-confidence and a very clear sense of identity; tends to speak plainly and isn’t concerned with appearing socially desirable. Cooperative warmth is not his default—he can be blunt, competitive, and skeptical of others’ motives—yet he values fairness and can be meaningfully generous when he decides it’s “equitable,” especially toward family and those he sees as deserving. Highly disciplined and practical, prefers simple/streamlined solutions and minimal clutter, and makes generally steady, not overly anxious decisions with moderate risk tolerance and some loss sensitivity. Intellectually engaged and knowledge-driven (likes complex reasoning and learning), open to new ideas and ambiguity, and more of a satisficer than a perfectionist. Environmentally minded and motivated by improvement and “making things better,” aspiring to be patient, helpful, and community-contributing, though he can disengage when bored and may reciprocate trust cautiously.

Young Hispanic Catholic woman in the U.S. South (18–29), moderate Democrat, part-time worker with an associate’s degree, living in a 4-person household and is a mother; values family/community and shows strong empathy, fairness, and generosity, tending to share evenly and to trust others while also being somewhat cautious about being treated unfairly. Quiet and socially awkward/introverted but highly curious, creative, and open to new ideas; prefers collaboration and harmony over standing out, with low need to be unique and a generally grounded, honest response style. Emotionally tends to overthink and can be moderately sensitive to stress, yet reports low anxiety/depressive symptoms overall. Decision-making: enjoys thinking and exploring possibilities and is comfortable with ambiguity, but often relies on intuition and may struggle with complex logic, numbers, and especially financial concepts; benefits from clear, simple, step-by-step guidance and practical examples for money decisions. Spending is slightly tightwad-leaning and uses mental “budgets” to organize gains/losses; aspires to be more confident, well-spoken, successful, and—given parenting responsibilities—more patient, responsible, and selfless.

Older widowed white woman in the Northeast, highly educated, retired, lives alone, Protestant and attends church weekly; politically liberal/Democrat with strong environmental values and a preference for simple, uncluttered living. Quiet and reserved rather than socially outgoing, generally kind and cooperative with decent empathy, but cautious and skeptical about others’ intentions—tends to withhold trust and be self-protective with money, even while valuing fairness and aspiring to be more generous. Very strong analytical and verbal reasoning skills, numerate and financially literate; enjoys thinking through complex issues, prefers clear answers and structure, and often optimizes decisions using mental “budgets” and categories. Emotionally can be prone to worry/negative affect despite low clinical anxiety/depression; self-aware, adaptable to social situations, and prefers fitting in over standing out.

Married Hispanic male in his 30s–40s living in the US South, college-educated, Protestant (weekly churchgoer), politically moderate/independent, working full-time with a mid-income household of four. Extremely outgoing, cooperative, disciplined, and curious, with very low anxiety and emotional volatility; enjoys thinking through complex issues and tends to be both relationship-oriented and achievement-driven. Values fairness and reciprocity in negotiations (generous offers, expects refusals of unfairness), is generally prosocial and trustworthy when in the “return” role, but is cautious about extending trust upfront. Strong environmental values and a preference for standing out; highly attuned to social cues and able to adapt presentation to context, yet has relatively shaky self-concept clarity and notably negative self-image. Decision style is analytical and optimizing, with strong general knowledge and reasoning, but weaker basic numeracy and a tendency to overrate his performance relative to others. Financially literate and risk-averse, uses mental “budgets,” and leans tight with spending; also shows impatience/present bias that can pull him toward short-term rewards despite long-term goals.

Young white woman in the US South (late teens/20s), some college, self-employed, mid-income, very liberal Democrat and nonreligious. Quiet and socially reserved, opens up only with trusted people and prefers a small circle over surface-level relationships. Highly anxious and somewhat prone to low mood, with a strong desire for certainty and clear answers; worries can drive decisions, and she values feeling calm, safe, and in control. Generally responsible and disciplined, fairness-minded, and moderately empathetic; she wants to be kind and courageous but not taken advantage of. Environmentally minded with a preference for simplicity/minimalism and a moderate need to feel unique. Tends to prefer straightforward, low-friction information rather than extended deliberation, yet can reason well when prompted; not especially overconfident. Financially she’s relatively willing to take risks and can be impatient for near-term rewards, but tries to ensure she “walks away with something.” In social/economic exchanges she’s trusting and inclined to share fairly while still protecting her own interests.

Young Hispanic man in the U.S. South (18–29), high‑school educated, living with a partner in a large household, working full time with a high income; agnostic, nonreligious, liberal/Democrat. He’s moderately outgoing and organized, emotionally somewhat reactive with elevated anxiety and depressive symptoms, and tends to present himself in a socially acceptable light. Strongly autonomy‑focused and equality‑minded, he openly prioritizes doing what he wants and being self‑reliant, with limited concern for standing out or conforming to group loyalty; he can be blunt/less cooperative and low in empathy, though he still thinks about fairness. Decision‑making is practical and numbers‑comfortable (high financial literacy/numeracy, good novel problem solving), but he doesn’t enjoy effortful thinking for its own sake and prefers to keep options open rather than seek quick closure; he can be reflective when needed and aims to optimize choices. Financially he’s relatively minimalist, uses mental “budgets,” is not especially impatient, and is comfortable with risk. Socially he is very trusting and generous upfront and accepts others’ offers, but when in control of resources he may reciprocate less and evaluates others based on perceived need and personal judgments.

Young Hispanic woman in the Western US, college-educated, liberal/Democrat, culturally Catholic but rarely attends, living in a small household and currently unemployed with mid–high income resources. Quiet and introverted with low interest in novelty or abstract “for fun” thinking; prefers familiar routines, simple/clear information, and quick takeaways. Emotionally sensitive with elevated anxiety/depressive tendencies, prone to overthinking and stress, and benefits from reassurance, structure, and low-pressure social settings; wants to become more confident socially and is motivated to improve despite discomfort. Moderately conscientious and organized, strongly prefers certainty and closure, and tends to “maximize” (can get stuck optimizing or second-guessing). Empathy and helpfulness are genuine, but trust and generosity depend on context: fair-minded in negotiated situations yet more self-protective when giving is purely voluntary or when the other party is unknown. Financially/numerically capable and not prone to overconfidence; tends to be cautious about spending and uses mental “budgets.” Values autonomy and equality over status/competition, leans minimalist, and is not especially driven by environmental concerns or standing out.

Married White Protestant woman in her 50s–early 60s living in the US South, postgraduate educated, working full-time with a mid-income household of three; politically conservative/Republican and moderately religiously active. Socially she is moderately outgoing but more blunt/guarded than warm, with very low expressed empathy and a tendency to prioritize practicality and self-protection over emotional attunement, though she does think about fairness and reciprocity. She prefers familiar routines over novelty, is not especially detail-disciplined, and can feel busy and overwhelmed; anxiety and low mood are prominent, alongside lower self-confidence and a less settled sense of self, which can make her second-guess and seek steadiness. Decision-wise she is highly risk-averse and strongly prefers immediate payoffs, is cautious about trusting others upfront but tends to reciprocate when treated fairly, and often offers the minimum she views as acceptable in one-shot splits. She is exceptionally strong with numbers and financial concepts, but less drawn to deep, effortful thinking or abstract reasoning; she responds best to clear, concrete choices and step-by-step guidance. She likes to feel distinctive and self-improving, aspires to be calmer and more patient, and values integrity, responsibility, and community contribution (including some environmental concern) more than trendiness or minimalism.

Divorced White woman in her 30s–40s living in the US South, politically liberal/Democrat, Protestant but rarely attends, lives alone and works full-time (some college, no degree; mid income). She is outgoing, warm, cooperative, and community-minded, with strong empathy and fairness norms—generous in sharing decisions but still attentive to her own payoff and prefers equitable splits. Highly conscientious and efficient at work, values honor, hard work, and service, and aspires to be ambitious without harming others; however, she often prioritizes downtime after work and feels some regret about not finishing schooling, contributing to a somewhat uncertain self-concept. Curious and open to new ideas, enjoys thinking through complex problems and can override gut reactions with reflective reasoning; tends to optimize rather than “good enough.” Emotionally steady overall but experiences elevated anxiety and some depressive symptoms. Financially, she is organized and uses mental budgets, is moderately impatient with a present-bias tilt, more sensitive to losses than gains, and not especially risk-averse; numeracy is strong but general financial literacy is weaker. She leans minimalist and environmentally friendly, is not strongly driven to be unique or to manage impressions, and is generally trusting and reciprocal while keeping boundaries.

Midwestern white woman in her 20s, married, college-educated, employed full time with a moderate Republican bent and low religious involvement. Socially warm and cooperative—values fairness, tends to be generous in sharing decisions, and is comfortable trusting others—while also highly image-aware and skilled at adjusting her behavior to fit social expectations (and may present herself in an especially socially desirable light). Curious, idea-open, and enjoys thinking through complex topics, with strong logical/verbal reasoning and financial knowledge, though less reliant on rote facts and sometimes prone to intuitive snap judgments unless prompted to slow down. Emotionally steady with very low anxiety/depressive tendency; generally optimistic and resilient. Decision style is ambitious and optimization-oriented: likes to compare options, seek the “best” choice, and tolerate ambiguity rather than rushing to closure; also prefers some simplicity/minimalism. Motivationally driven by goals and improvement, fairly disciplined/organized, and willing to take risks; tends to be more tightwad than spendthrift. Strong desire to stand out and be unique, yet has relatively fluid/uncertain self-concept, so preferences and identity may shift with context and new experiences.

Widowed Midwestern woman (30–49) living alone, some college, working part-time on a modest income; politically moderate/independent and nonreligious. Quiet and low-key socially (more reserved than outgoing) but warm, cooperative, and highly reliable—organized, self-disciplined, and comfortable taking responsibility. Values humility and fairness, prefers simple/minimal possessions, and strongly cares about helping others and the environment; tends to be very generous and reciprocal, yet also has firm boundaries against unfair treatment. Thinks things through and enjoys complex topics, likes hearing both sides, and prefers clear answers over ambiguity, but generally “satisficies” rather than obsessively optimizing. Emotionally fairly steady with mild anxiety/depressive tendencies; self-concept is clear and improving, with growing confidence after loss and a focus on meeting challenges head-on. Independent-minded and equality-oriented, with a noticeable desire to be distinctive rather than blend in; not highly image-managing in the moment, though can answer in socially acceptable ways.

Black male in his 30s–40s in the Western US, college-educated, moderate/independent, nonreligious, living with one other person and working full-time with a solid middle income. Quiet, reserved, and somewhat shy, he prefers low-key influence over overt social dominance, aspiring to be a thoughtful, grounded, “quiet but inspirational” leader and a moderating, dependable role model. He is cooperative and fairness-minded (often considers others’ needs and social norms), generally trusting and generous in resource-sharing, but can be selective about what he will accept when terms feel unfair. Curious and imaginative with a strong preference for thinking through complex ideas, he also wants clear pathways and can struggle to complete large, unstructured tasks; overall he is very dependable and duty-oriented but may bog down when ambiguity is high. Decision-making tends toward optimizing and seeking closure/certainty; he likes structure, mental budgets, and minimalist simplicity. Emotionally he is mostly steady with some elevated anxiety and occasional self-doubt, and his self-concept can feel less settled, which can increase sensitivity to evaluation; he can adapt his presentation to context. He values autonomy with an egalitarian streak, while also emphasizing loyalty and responsibility to the group. Financially and behaviorally he leans toward risk-taking and impatience for delayed rewards, shows a spendthrift tendency, and can be highly confident in his judgments relative to actual performance—benefiting from feedback, guardrails, and concrete metrics when stakes are high.

Black male (30–49) in the US South; never married, Protestant but attends a few times a year; politically independent but generally liberal; some college, works part-time with low income and a two-person household. Socially outgoing, warm, and highly cooperative, with strong empathy and a pronounced fairness norm—prefers even splits, is willing to trust and reciprocate, and avoids being seen as unfair. Curious and idea-open with a high enjoyment of thinking through problems; adapts well to new situations and stays calm under stress with low anxiety/depressive tendencies and a clear sense of self. Moderately organized but not rigid; motivated both by personal advancement and (especially) maintaining relationships and group harmony, leaning toward egalitarian, interdependent values rather than status competition. Decision style is generally reflective but can be overconfident; prefers certainty and is moderately optimizing. Financially, tends to compartmentalize money, is risk-averse, has low numeracy/financial literacy, and shows strong impatience/present bias—more likely to favor immediate, concrete benefits and may struggle with long-term planning despite good reasoning potential. Not strongly minimalist, not particularly driven to stand out, somewhat attentive to social impressions, and only mildly environmentally oriented. Aspires to reach and entertain people (make them laugh) while being calm, hardworking, and dedicated to his vision.

White, married, self-employed woman in her 50s–60s living in the U.S. South; moderate Democrat and agnostic, not religiously involved, in a two-person, high-income household with some college. Interpersonally warm, cooperative, loyal, and fairness-minded, she tends to help others while still keeping practical boundaries and slightly favoring herself in splits; she’s moderately trusting and generally even-handed. She’s more reserved than outgoing and not highly image-managing, with a clear sense of who she is (kind, funny, a bit sarcastic) and low need to stand out. Decision-making is deliberate and logical with strong learned knowledge and good rule-based reasoning, though she prefers straightforward information over lengthy, abstract analysis; she’s comfortable with ambiguity and less driven by quick closure. She’s highly conscientious and planful, somewhat risk-averse, and uses clear mental “budgets,” yet can be tempted toward overspending and may second-guess choices due to a tendency to optimize. Values emphasize relationships and community over status, with a modest environmental lean and a preference for simpler, less cluttered living. Motivations center on financial stability/independence, being present with family, and personal creativity (watercolor/card design) and travel; mood can run somewhat anxious or down at times but generally stays steady.

Midwestern married White woman in her 20s with an associate’s degree, full-time job, and comfortable household income; Protestant and liberal/Democrat with strong environmental values. She is highly empathetic, cooperative, and conscientious, with high curiosity and enjoyment of complex thinking; emotionally steady and low in anxiety/depression. Interpersonally she presents as kind and socially attuned (very image-aware and good at adjusting behavior to context), but is guarded with trust and reciprocity—quick to protect her own interests and reluctant to give without assurance, and she admits she struggles to forgive or forget when wronged despite aspiring to be more trusting. Decision-wise she is a strong optimizer who tolerates ambiguity and keeps options open, prefers simple/minimalist choices, and can reason reflectively, but may lack confidence/skill with numbers and practical financial concepts. Money behavior is mixed: she tends toward impulsive spending and present-focused temptation, yet also uses mental “buckets” for budgeting; generally moderate on risk. She values both independence and group loyalty, seeks to stand out and be unique, and may give responses that sound socially desirable even when her actions are more self-protective.

Married white Catholic man in his 30s–40s in the Northeast with a postgraduate education, high income, and full-time job; politically moderate Democrat who attends church occasionally. He is highly conscientious, disciplined, and achievement-oriented, with strong knowledge, numeracy, and analytic reasoning, and he prefers structured decisions—seeking certainty, optimizing choices, and feeling uncomfortable with ambiguity. Socially he is more reserved than outgoing and can come across as blunt or less naturally accommodating, yet he holds strong fairness and generosity norms: he tends to give others a meaningful share and trusts readily, though he’s less inclined to reciprocate at the same level when roles reverse. Emotionally he is prone to anxiety and negative self-evaluation, is sensitive to potential losses, and can be impatient for near-term rewards; he often frames goals around responsibility, resilience, and providing for family, with a self-aware drive for self-improvement rather than a desire to stand out.
